title: Reduce metric cardinality for A/B experiment metrics by enforcing tag allowlist
author: Allison Grant
description: Context: Route-level A/B testing adds experiment_id/variant_id dimensions to latency/cost/error metrics. During dogfood we saw a sharp increase in series count due to free-form tags (route path, model string variants, and accidental propagation of request headers). This PR tightens the tag set for all experiment-scoped metrics and enforces an allowlist at emission time to prevent high-cardinality explosions while preserving the dimensions needed for Console reporting and dashboards. Changes: (1) Introduce a single canonical allowlist for experiment metric tags (experiment_id, variant, route_id, region, project_id, status_class, transport, streaming). (2) Normalize values (length caps, character set, status class bucketing) and reject unknown tags. (3) Add drop counters and rate-limited logs when tags are removed so we can detect regressions without spamming. (4) Update gateway + cost attribution emitters to use the new tag builder, and add unit tests + a small integration test for series count. Rollout: gated behind feature flag ab_metrics_tag_allowlist_v1 default ON in staging, then 10% production for 24h before global enable. Notes: this does not change exposure events (those remain structured events with their own schema/versioning); this only affects metrics time series tags. Checklist: added tests; validated dashboards still render; verified no PII tags; perf impact <1µs/request in benchmark; added migration note for Grafana queries using old tag keys.
commits: gateway: route AB metrics through allowlisted tag builder
metering: cost attribution metrics use normalized experiment tag set
tests: series-count guard + golden tests for tag normalization
docs: note tag key deprecations for internal dashboards

Grafana query templates (internal) / notes for dashboard maintainers
snippets: Rust (new allowlist + normalization): pub const EXPERIMENT_METRIC_TAGS_ALLOWLIST: &[&str] = &["experiment_id","variant","route_id","region","project_id","status_class","transport","streaming"];
Rust (dropping unknown tags): if !allowlist.contains(&k.as_str()) { dropped += 1; continue; }
Rust (status bucketing): let status_class = format!("{}xx", status / 100);
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry/analytics): "Can we confirm we’re not breaking the results aggregation jobs that group by route + variant? Those jobs expect route today." Allison Grant (author): "Yes—route becomes route_id (stable hashed identifier), and we keep a mapping table already produced by routing configs. I added a note in docs/internal/observability/ab-testing-metric-tags.md and verified the aggregation query uses route_id in staging." Nadia Rahman (Cost attribution): "Cost metrics currently tag model_name and quant_profile; are we dropping those? We still need per-variant cost comparisons." Allison: "We’re dropping model_name and quant_profile specifically from the experiment-scoped metrics to keep series bounded; the per-variant comparison still works because variant implies config (model + params) in the experiment definition. For deeper breakdowns, cost attribution remains available in non-experiment dashboards and traces." Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Please add a metric for dropped tags and alerting guidance. If we start dropping required tags due to bugs we’ll silently lose sliceability." Allison: "Added redwood.telemetry.metric_tags_dropped_total{scope="experiment"} and a rate-limited log line keyed by metric name. I also added a quick runbook note in the doc for checking this counter during rollout." Caleb Johnson (Tracing/metrics ingestion): "Do we enforce length caps to avoid pathological values (e.g., route header dumping)?" Allison: "Yes, caps at 64 chars per value and ASCII whitelist; anything else gets replaced with "_" and counted as normalized." Approvals: Logan approved after verifying dashboards; Nadia approved after confirming cost comparisons remain; Sean approved with rollout plan; Caleb approved with note to follow up on shared helper reuse for non-experiment metrics.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit message: "Reduce metric cardinality for A/B experiment metrics by enforcing tag allowlist (#18519)"
release_notes: Internal: Experiment-scoped metrics now emit only allowlisted tags (experiment_id, variant, route_id, region, project_id, status_class, transport, streaming). Any dashboards querying deprecated keys (route, model_name, quant_profile) should be updated to use route_id/variant. Added dropped-tag counter redwood.telemetry.metric_tags_dropped_total{scope="experiment"} for rollout monitoring.
